destination.name: Alice Springs
destination.tagline: The Red Centre's hub among the MacDonnell Ranges, with a desert wildlife park, a telegraph station and sacred gaps on its doorstep.
destination.description: Alice Springs (Mparntwe) sits among the MacDonnell Ranges in the middle of Australia and is the base for the Red Centre. The town grew around the 1872 Overland Telegraph Station, which can still be visited, and its museums cover the Flying Doctor, The Ghan railway and the road trains. A hilltop memorial, a botanic garden and the sacred gaps of the Heavitree Range are minutes from the centre, and the Desert Park shows the region's wildlife. The East and West MacDonnell Ranges are reached by road from here.
whyVisit: Watch the bird show at the Desert Park
Look over town from Anzac Hill

goodToKnow.title: Check opening days
goodToKnow.detail: Several museums close on set days: the Women's Museum is shut Sunday and Monday, and the Road Transport Museum is shut Saturday.

goodToKnow.title: Hot days, cold nights
goodToKnow.detail: Summer days are very hot and winter nights can fall below freezing. Plan walks for early morning and pack layers in winter.

goodToKnow.title: Respect sacred sites
goodToKnow.detail: At Emily Gap, traditional owners ask visitors not to climb the rocks or photograph the rock art. Follow signs at other sites.
